text:
acme_integration: Hi, after the 11:00 UTC rollout our ingest pipeline started failing schema validation. Parser expects {"order":..., "items":[...] } but we're seeing extra top-level keys intermittently. Example request body: ```{\n  "order": {"id": 1234},\n  "items": [...],\n  "debug_meta": {"source": "llm"},\n  "x_source_id": "abc-987"\n}```
maya: ugh, thanks for reporting — can you paste the exact request_id or a full raw payload? :pray:
acme_integration: sample attached, request_id=req_01G7Z2A4, shipping logs show JSON parse error: "unexpected field 'debug_meta'". Reproduces ~30% of responses.
sam_eng: noting this — deploy-bot shows the canary flip to model v2.3 happened at 10:58 UTC. tagging eng-ml and infra.
jordan_cs: looping in leo_ml and sam_eng. customer is blocked; high impact. can we prioritize a quick rollback or a mitigant?
deploy-bot: blue-green deploy completed for service=runtime-canary, id=deploy-2024-11-06-1058
leo_ml: I pulled the sample. Looks like some outputs now include an extra envelope-like object. Possibly our structured-output wrapper is being emitted as top-level fields for certain prompts. repro steps: run prompt set "order_v1" against model v2.3 with streaming disabled.
maya: is there any change in the response content-type or preface? we saw earlier issues where wrappers got serialized into the main body.
acme_integration: response headers look same (application/json) — parser fails because it doesn't expect x_source_id at the same level. It used to be inside metadata.
sam_eng: quick test: calling /v1/generate with model=v2.3 and prompt id=order_v1 -> I get extra key `debug_meta` in ~1/4 runs. logging trace: ```RESPONSE SNIPPET:
{ "order": {...}, "items": [...], "debug_meta": ":::" }
``` seems non-deterministic.
leo_ml: hypothesis: rollout enabled a new structured-output path that sometimes returns a sparse metadata object at top-level instead of under `meta`. Probable bug in serializer mapping when output-null suppression kicks in.
jordan_cs: customer asked for workaround — can we offer them a temporary schema-tolerant parser suggestion?
maya: suggest toggling strict_schema validation off for that ingest route OR add a small pre-parse step to drop unexpected keys: `payload.pop('debug_meta', None)` until we fix. communicate risk.
acme_integration: can we get ETA? We're seeing 15% downstream failures, customer on-call is upset.
leo_ml: short-term: enable fallback that strips known extra keys. Mid-term: roll back v2.3 canary to v2.2 for affected region or patch serializer mapping. I'll try a patch to force metadata nesting.
sam_eng: I've queued a rollback for the canary in eu-west-1 and rolled forward a hotfix toggle in runtime to keep old envelope behavior. Will monitor.
maya: tagging the customer: "we've applied a temporary ingest workaround and are rolling back the canary in affected regions. we'll follow up with a postmortem." :thumbsup:
acme_integration: confirmed — after strip step parser success rate back to 99%. thanks team.
leo_ml: filing follow-up issue for ml-runtime: serializer mapping + unit test for nested metadata. will include stable test prompts and a regression harness.
jordan_cs: thanks all — I'll update the customer and close the ticket once rollback is stable.
